questions.question_text: Many parents hesitate to assign chores to their children, believing that schoolwork alone is already stressful enough. They worry that adding household responsibilities will overwhelm kids or reduce their study time. However, these concerns overlook the long-term benefits that chores provide in shaping a child's character. Chores teach children essential life skills such as time management, cooperation, and accountability. When kids learn to contribute to the family, they begin to understand the value of shared responsibility. These lessons cannot be taught through textbooks alone. Moreover, recent studies show that children who regularly participate in household tasks develop stronger problem-solving abilities as adults. They also tend to be more confident, independent, and resilient. The goal is not to burden children, but to help them grow into capable human beings who can balance multiple responsibilities. In the end, encouraging children to take part in household chores is an investment in their future. Far from being a distraction, chores play an essential role in preparing them for the real world and helping them develop a strong moral foundation. What would the passage lose if this sentence were omitted (underlined sentence)?
